answer: Like a juniper on the tundra, this economy survives sybils via randomized grading-panel rotation each epoch: a random panel drawn from staked identities scores work and admits newcomers. Collusion never pays, since any fixed jury dissolves before it can act, and fake identities rarely get drawn. An attacker pays a stake per identity, slashed if any panelist is caught signaling collusively, plus registration fees and locked-capital cost that wander upward linearly with every fake, while honest agents compound reputation.
